key_insight: This work demonstrates a feasible mapping of classical Sobel-based edge detection and a Harris-style corner detector into quantum circuits by using two quantum image encoding schemes, enabling gradient and corner response computation on quantum hardware.
problem_solved: Brings gradient-based edge and corner detection into the quantum domain by addressing how to encode images, implement Sobel kernels as quantum operators, and compute a Harris-style corner response under quantum measurement and resource constraints.
method: Encode images into quantum states using two quantum image representation schemes (authors evaluate two encodings).
Realize Sobel kernels as quantum operators to compute horizontal/vertical gradients and gradient magnitude in superposition.
Form a Harris-style corner response from the quantum-computed gradients and recover edge/corner locations via measurement and classical post-processing.
impact: Provides a practical blueprint for basic computer-vision primitives on quantum devices, opening a path to integrate edge/corner detection into quantum ML and image-processing pipelines and to study trade-offs in qubit/gate resources, noise, and accuracy.
visual_elements: Quantum circuit diagram illustrating the Sobel operator implementation and gradient extraction gates.
Three-panel image example: original image | quantum-derived edge map | quantum-detected corners overlaid.
Pipeline flowchart: image encoding → quantum filtering (Sobel) → corner response (Harris) → measurement & classical post-processing.
Compact resource/metrics chart comparing qubit count, gate depth, and detection quality (quantum variants vs classical baseline).
paper_title: Quantum Gradient-Based Approach for Edge and Corner Detection Using Sobel Kernels
paper_authors: Mohammad Aamir Sohail, Gabriela Pinheiro, Yasemin Poyraz Kocak, Batuhan Hangun, Emre Camkerten
